title: TRILUME / REPETITION BUILDS FORM
core_formula: ordinary repeated part -> regular spacing -> shared structure -> visual rhythm -> collectible object
core_lesson: ONE WEAK ELEMENT CAN BECOME STRONG THROUGH REPETITION.
secondary_lesson: DON'T DESIGN EVERY PART - DESIGN THE RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN PARTS.
summary: Repeated discarded steel cans become a coherent pendant light when aligned, evenly spaced, connected by a shared reclaimed beam and treated as modules rather than individual objects.
learn: Treat repeated found objects as modules before redesigning them individually.
ONE IS AN OBJECT. MANY CAN BECOME A MATERIAL.
Repetition needs a rule: size, interval, axis, direction, count and shared structure.
Design can live in relationships between parts rather than in each part.
A shared structure can create identity from weak individual components.
Preserve visible provenance instead of disguising the cans.
Repetition can increase visual value without erasing origin.
avoid: exactly three cans as a fixed rule
matte black as a mandatory finish
reclaimed wood beam as the only support
pendant lighting as the only application
horizontal linear composition as the only layout
failure_modes: repetition has no clear spacing or alignment rule and reads as clutter
the cans are over-disguised and provenance is lost
the shared support does not visually unify the modules
the object becomes generic industrial lighting rather than a found-material system
too many modules weaken the silhouette instead of strengthening rhythm
electrical implementation is treated as decorative craft rather than real mains-powered hardware
safety_notes: Use appropriately rated insulated lampholders and heat-safe components.
Provide secure strain relief and mechanically protected wiring.
Metal housings require an appropriate grounding or double-insulation strategy according to local electrical standards.
The Taste Library concept is not a substitute for certified electrical engineering or code compliance.
